prompt:
Paint the COMPLETE top-down map of a very unusual fantasy DESERT OASIS TOWN as ONE finished game map image, in rich premium modern hi-bit pixel art (the "HD pixel art" JRPG look: hand-placed crisp square pixels, hue-shifted ramps, dark warm outlines), flat classic top-down RPG map view (NOT an HD-2D diorama, no depth-of-field, no tilt-shift, no 3D render).

THE TOWN: "Kasim", an old caravan town that grew in a hollow between tall sand dunes, at the feet of a COLOSSAL SEATED STONE STATUE of a forgotten king, half buried in the northern dune. The statue's face has been worn completely smooth by centuries of sandstorms (no eyes, no mouth: a blank, eerie oval), and it wears a long striped royal head-cloth. It is NOT an ordinary town: there are NO square houses, nothing is arranged in rows or on a grid, and there are no brick or timber boxes. People live and trade in strange organic shapes: clusters of round sun-baked mud DOMES, a giant toppled CLAY JAR, a hall made of the huge bleached RIBCAGE of an ancient beast covered with dyed cloth, a dwelling carved into a lone sandstone ROCK, a pigeon tower, wind-catcher towers and granary domes. Narrow earthen lanes wind organically between them. The spring of the town lies in the upturned PALM of a gigantic STONE HAND that broke off the statue long ago and lies in the middle of the square.

The attached image is an exact LAYOUT GUIDE (trace over it: your painting will be laid pixel-for-pixel on top of it and checked against it, so do not shift, shrink, mirror or re-arrange anything; keep every edge within a few pixels of the guide) drawn on a 62 x 56 tile grid (each tile = 48 x 48 px of the output, output is 2976 x 2688). Every shape must sit exactly where it is in the guide at the same size: this image is used directly as the walkable game map, so positions are collision data.

Guide colour key:
- orange with wavy lines = TALL SAND DUNES all around the town (not walkable): big smooth rolling dunes with wind ripples, sharp crests and soft shaded lee sides, a few dry grass tufts; they rise around the town like a bowl. The two gaps at the left and right edges are the town gates (see below).
- pale sand = the walkable sandy ground of the town: packed, fine pale sand with footprints, faint wind ripples, small pebbles, a few flat stones and dry tufts. FLAT ground detail only.
- red-brown = narrow winding EARTH LANES of trodden reddish clay (walkable): cracked, a few flat stepping slabs, worn ruts, soft natural wavy edges (you may round off the blocky corners of the guide a little, but stay inside the red-brown area).
- light grey squares = the old PAVED SQUARE of big worn sandstone flagstones (walkable), a faint sun-ray pattern radiating from the stone hand in the middle, sand drifted into the joints. FLAT.
- green circles = small groves of DATE PALMS seen from above (not walkable): lush fan crowns with orange date clusters, shade under them.
- the big brown mass at the top = the COLOSSAL SEATED STATUE of the king seen from above/front, carved from warm sandstone and half sunk in the dune: the round light oval near the top is its WORN BLANK FACE (smooth, featureless, cracked, sand streaks), the striped shape around it is the long striped royal head-cloth falling onto its broad shoulders, below come its huge shoulders and chest, then its knees and a wide carved PLINTH (the lighter horizontal ledge). Chips, cracks, sand drifts on its shoulders, a few ropes and faded cloth banners hanging from it.
- the three lighter panels at the bottom of the statue = the FRONT FACE OF THE PLINTH, where three shops are cut into the stone, each with its own carved doorway (black mark) and a small window: left = the item shop, middle = the fortune teller, right = the map maker. Carved reliefs of caravans and camels between them; the NAME CARTOUCHE in the plinth's centre has been chiselled away (a rough scar).
- the ring of pale stone squares in the middle of the paved square = the STONE HAND: a gigantic broken-off stone hand of the statue lying PALM-UP on the pavement, its fingers curled up towards the statue (the finger stubs at the top), the thumb on the left, the broken wrist at the bottom. The pale squares are its fingers, thumb and the raised rim of the palm (not walkable). The red-brown area inside is the HOLLOW OF THE PALM: an almost dry spring basin of cracked mud with ancient carved letters on the bottom, and the small blue patch is the last shallow puddle of clear water. There is an opening at the wrist (bottom middle) where people step down into the palm.
- the cluster at top left = the INN "Star of the Spring": three fused round white-washed mud DOMES seen from above, with a tall square WIND-CATCHER tower between them topped by a star-shaped brass lantern cage (the yellow star); the lighter rounded band below is its curved front wall with the door and small round windows.
- the orange-red oval at top right = the TAVERN: a GIANT TOPPLED CLAY WINE JAR lying on its side in the sand (terracotta, painted bands and zigzags, a chipped neck and mouth on the east end), with a door and little windows cut into its belly (the band at its bottom).
- the round dome at the right with the wooden wheel = the WELL-DIGGER'S HOUSE: a white mud dome with a curved front wall, and a big wooden water-lifting wheel with clay pots standing against its east side.
- the blue shape with white arches at the bottom right = the CARAVAN GUILD: a long hall made of the enormous bleached RIBCAGE and spine of an ancient beast half sunk in the sand, the ribs arching over it, covered with stretched INDIGO and MADDER-RED dyed cloth and rugs; its front (the red band) is a hanging cloth-and-timber wall with the door.
- the brown shape at left = the TOMB KEEPER'S DWELLING carved into a lone weathered sandstone rock covered in carved glyphs; its front is a dressed rock face with the door.
- the plain domes at the bottom = a round WATER CISTERN dome and three GRANARY domes (no doors: smooth plastered domes with small vents); the small round tower with dark dots = a PIGEON TOWER (dovecote) studded with nest holes; the square tower at the right = a WIND-CATCHER tower with dark vent slots (no door).
- small BLACK rectangles = the front DOORS. Each door must be painted exactly at that spot and size (a wooden or cloth-curtained door, bottom edge on the bottom edge of the wall). Do not add any other door or opening that looks like a door anywhere.
- small yellow squares = small windows (panes softly warm, but no glow spilling out).
- far left and right at the middle: the two TOWN GATES: the lanes leave the map between the dunes; mark each gate with two short mud-brick gate pillars with faded banners standing ON THE DUNE right beside the lane (not on the lane).
Buildings, statue, hand, palms and dunes must not extend outside their guide shapes (roofs and domes may bulge out by at most a few pixels).

Make everything rich, detailed, handcrafted and cohesive, like a lovingly painted JRPG town map of a dusty, fading oasis: sun-bleached plaster, terracotta, carved sandstone, faded indigo and madder cloth, brass, palm fibre ropes. Warm sand and ochre tones with indigo and turquoise accents. Details on walkable ground must stay flat (no tall things on the walkable areas).

Pixel art rules: crisp square pixels, no blur, no anti-aliasing, no painterly brush strokes, no noise, clear clusters, hue-shifted ramps, dark warm outlines on buildings. Characters in this game are about 140 output px tall, so details should be at that scale.
Lighting: this is the ALBEDO base layer. Neutral, soft, even daylight-like light; NO night, NO cast shadows longer than a few pixels, NO lamp light pools, NO glow, NO vignette, NO fog.
Do NOT paint any characters, animals, camels, lamp posts, braziers, barrels, crates, sacks, jars on the ground, market stalls, tents, signs, chests, text, labels, grid lines or UI. Leave open ground for them.
